abstract: BACKGROUND: Because metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell cancer is a rare but treatable cancer, we have explored whether there is an association between the experience of the treating institution with this disease and the long-term clinical outcome of the patients, particularly patients with a poor prognosis. METHODS: We analyzed data on 380 patients treated in one of 49 institutions participating in the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer/ Medical Research Council randomized trial of four cycles of bleomycin-etoposide-cisplatin followed by two cycles of etoposide-cisplatin versus three cycles of bleomycin-vincristine-cisplatin followed by three cycles of etoposide-ifosfamide-cisplatin-bleomycin, both treatment regimens given with or without filgrastim (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor). Institutions were divided into four groups based on the total number of patients entered in the trial. The groups were compared by use of the Cox proportional hazards model stratified for treatment with filgrastim and for patient prognosis as defined by the International Germ Cell Consensus Classification Group. With the use of this classification, only 65 % of the patients had a poor prognosis. RESULTS: Patients treated in the 26 institutions that entered fewer than five patients into the trial had an overall survival that was statistically significantly worse (two-sided P = .010; hazard ratio = 1.85; 95% confidence interval = 1.16-3.03) than that of patients treated in the 23 institutions that entered five patients or more. Overall survival and failure-free survival were similar among institutions that entered at least five patients. The observed effect may be related to differences in adherence to the chemotherapy protocol and in the frequency and extent of surgery for residual masses, although only the differences in dose intensity achieved statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: Patients treated in institutions that entered fewer than five patients into the trial appeared to have poorer survival than those treated in institutions that entered a larger number of patients with "poor-prognosis" nonseminoma.
abstract_ja: 背景:予後不良の転移性非セミノーマ胚細胞腫瘍は稀だが治療可能ながんである。施設での経験と長期的な臨床転帰の関連を検討した。方法:EORTC/MRC無作為化試験に参加した49施設で治療を受けた380例のデータを解析した。試験では、ブレオマイシン-エトポシド-シスプラチンを4サイクル行い、その後エトポシド-シスプラチンを2サイクル行うレジメンと、ブレオマイシン-ビンクリスチン-シスプラチンを3サイクル行い、その後エトポシド-イホスファミド-シスプラチン-ブレオマイシンを3サイクル行うレジメンを比較した。いずれも顆粒球コロニー刺激因子の有無で実施された。施設は試験への総登録患者数に基づいて4群に分けた。群間比較には、フィルグラスチムの使用と国際胚細胞腫瘍コンセンサス分類グループの予後分類で層別したCox比例ハザードモデルを用いた。この分類では患者の65%のみが予後不良であった。結果:試験への登録が5例未満の26施設で治療を受けた患者は、5例以上の23施設で治療を受けた患者に比べ、全生存期間が統計的に有意に不良であった(両側P=.010、ハザード比1.85、95%信頼区間1.16-3.03)。5例以上を登録した施設間では、全生存期間と無増悪生存期間は類似していた。この効果は、化学療法プロトコールの遵守度や残存腫瘤に対する手術の頻度と程度の差と関連している可能性があるが、統計学的に有意であったのは投与量強度の差のみであった。結論:試験への登録が5例未満の施設で治療を受けた患者は、より多くの患者を登録した施設の患者に比べて、予後不良の非セミノーマ胚細胞腫瘍の生存が不良であるようであった。
